short: a generic type used without type arguments, like List instead of List<String>. compiles for old code, switches the type checks off.
javac telling you it can't verify a generic operation, so a cast it inserted elsewhere might fail at run time.
the T in class Box<T>: a placeholder type. the String in Box<String> is the type argument.
javac working out a generic call's type arguments from the arguments and the target type.
<T extends Number>: callers may only pick Number or a subtype, and the code can call Number's methods on T.
? in a type argument: List<?>, List<? extends T> (read only) or List<? super T> (write only).
List<Integer> is not a List<Number>, even though Integer is a Number. generics are invariant, arrays are covariant.
javac naming the unknown type behind a ? (CAP#1 in errors). a generic helper method can capture it as a real T.
a synthetic method javac adds so overriding still works after erasure, like compareTo(Object) calling your compareTo(Name).
a String[] is an Object[], so every array store is checked at run time and can throw ArrayStoreException.
a variable of a parameterized type pointing at an object that isn't that type. caused by raw types, unchecked casts, generic varargs.
where a class file keeps generic types of classes, fields and methods after erasure. reflection reads it.
an anonymous subclass like new TypeRef<List<String>>() {} that captures a full generic type at run time.
a Class<T> passed in so generic code has a real type to check and cast with at run time.
